record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Computational Geometry
record.context_brief: Maximum matching in unit disk or square graphs
record.original_question: Given n unit disks, or n axis-parallel unit squares, in the plane, define the intersection graph with one vertex for each geometric object and an edge between two distinct objects exactly when they intersect. Can a maximum matching in this geometric intersection graph be computed in near-linear time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider one of the following two families of geometric objects in the Euclidean plane:
(a) a collection of n unit disks (closed disks of radius 1, with arbitrary centers), or
(b) a collection of n axis-parallel unit squares (closed squares of side length 1, with arbitrary positions).

For such a collection, define the intersection graph G whose vertex set is the n geometric objects and in which two distinct objects are joined by an edge if and only if they have a nonempty intersection. A matching in G is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges, and a maximum matching is a matching of maximum cardinality.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given the collection of n objects as input, computes a maximum matching in the intersection graph G in near-linear time, i.e., in time n · polylog(n)?
artifact.category_tag: Geometric intersection graphs / maximum matching algorithms
artifact.status_search_result: Best known exact algorithms for maximum matching in unit-disk intersection graphs achieve subquadratic time of order O(n^{ω/2}) via algebraic/separator methods (Bonnet, Cabello, Mulzer, 2020; published in Discrete & Computational Geometry 2023), and (1−ε)-approximation algorithms run in near-linear time (Har-Peled and Yang, SoCG 2022). No exact near-linear-time algorithm for maximum matching in unit disk or axis-parallel unit square intersection graphs is known, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Matchings in Geometric Intersection Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A maximum matching in an intersection graph G of n geometric objects can be found in O(ρ^{3ω/2} n^{ω/2}) time...
status_evidence.claim: Best known exact algorithms are subquadratic (n^{ω/2}-type), not near-linear.

status_evidence.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Matchings in Geometric Intersection Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: (1−ε)-approximation for maximum matching in disk graphs in near-linear time.
status_evidence.claim: Only approximation, not exact, achieves near-linear time.
